cohort: The study included 144 participants with singleton cephalic pregnancies at 37 weeks gestation or more, who delivered vaginally at a single tertiary perinatal center in Japan, with a second cohort requiring forceps delivery also analyzed.
finding: The TUS station correlated with DVE findings for fetal head descent and showed utility as an objective parameter for assessing labour progression and predicting forceps delivery difficulty.
mod_finding: The TUS station was found to be a valuable and objective parameter for consideration in decisions regarding forceps delivery difficulty.
